newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng hits record high in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng hits record high in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose to a new record high during early trade on Wednesday boosted by optimism over the direction of interest rates, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was up 104 points at 12,910.85 after hitting an all-time high at 12,913.47.
"Hong Kong is going up in line with Wall Street, but more importantly Hong Kong has a lack of sellers, said Francis Wong, executive director at DBS Securities in Hong Kong.
Turnover which was modest at the open rose to a robust HK$1.57 billion in the first 40 minutes of trade.
"This market has few competitors for funds. People are more keen to chase after momentum, than to settle down and bottom fish in other markets," Wong added.
Brokers and analysts agreed that the market was high but still offered value.
"We believe investors should continue to focus on quality, research carefully before buying laggards," said Amy Wong, research director at New China Hong Kong.

At 12,800, the market is trading on 14.4 times 1996 earnings, said Wong, adding the brokerage house was forecasting 13.0 percent earnings growth for the Hang Seng Index for next year, putting the market on a PER of 13.0 times 1997 earnings.
The market's strength also comes from the favourable outlook for interest rates in the coming three months.
"The (U.S.) bond market was strong and is supporting the market," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales executive at NAVA SC Securities.
The U.S. 30-year treasury bond yield fell to a bullish 6.44 percent, while the Dow gained 10.44 points to hit another record closing high of 6,266.04.
The market's record breaking advance was led by interest-rate sensitive issues, property counters and banks.
The rally in general was centered on blue chips, and mid cap issues and H shares lagged the index, brokers said.
International banking giant and index heavyweight HSBC Holdings jumped HK$1.50 to HK$162.00. Sun Hung Kai Properties led its sector with a gain of HK$1.25 to HK$89.75.
